headline: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 652 as 4 children die in 24 hours
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reports a surge in both confirmed and suspected cases across Bangladesh, with Dhaka Division seeing the most fatalities.
details: Four more children with measles symptoms have died within a 24-hour period, bringing the total death toll to 652.
According to the DGHS, 92 deaths have been confirmed from the disease since March 15, while 570 people with suspected cases have also died.
The Dhaka Division has recorded the highest number of deaths at 236, followed by Rajshahi Division with 87 fatalities.
In the last 24 hours alone, 1,052 people with measles symptoms sought treatment at hospitals, with 973 of them being admitted.
Dhaka hospitals have seen the most admissions, with 398 patients, while Rangpur has the lowest number of admissions at 12.
The overall count of confirmed measles cases in the country has reached 10,323, while suspected cases have risen to 85,951.

headline: 87,000 teacher appointments and promotions stalled by legal hurdles
summary: Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon reveals that litigation and bureaucratic complications are blocking thousands of positions in the primary education sector.
details: Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon stated that nearly 87,000 teaching and school leadership positions across Bangladesh are tied up in legal and administrative complications.
The primary education sector is currently grappling with around 40,000 vacant teaching positions, while recruitment for another 47,000 roles has been stalled by litigation.
Specifically, the appointment of approximately 32,500 head teachers has been delayed for over three years due to unresolved court cases.
The minister noted that nearly 83,000 cases involving the education ministry are pending before the courts, which severely constrains decision-making.
Milon also criticized the interim government for a rushed recruitment of 14,500 primary school teachers, questioning the quality of the selection process.
The government is currently reviewing these recruitments and has appointed the selected candidates on two-year pro-contracts while they undergo training.
To improve learning outcomes, the government plans to incorporate sports and cultural education into the curriculum and has increased the education budget to 2 percent of the national budget.
caption:
Nearly 87,000 teacher positions are frozen in Bangladesh. Court cases and bureaucracy are blocking the future of our classrooms.

Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon stated that nearly 87,000 teaching and school leadership positions across Bangladesh are tied up in legal and administrative complications.

The primary education sector is currently grappling with around 40,000 vacant teaching positions, while recruitment for another 47,000 roles has been stalled by litigation.

Specifically, the appointment of approximately 32,500 head teachers has been delayed for over three years due to unresolved court cases.

The minister noted that nearly 83,000 cases involving the education ministry are pending before the courts, which severely constrains decision-making.

Milon also criticized the interim government for a rushed recruitment of 14,500 primary school teachers, questioning the quality of the selection process.

The government is currently reviewing these recruitments and has appointed the selected candidates on two-year pro-contracts while they undergo training.

To improve learning outcomes, the government plans to incorporate sports and cultural education into the curriculum and has increased the education budget to 2 percent of the national budget.
